StartUp Health, a global network of founders and CEOs committed to achieving health moonshots, is now accepting applications from founders at all stages — from preclinical to those scaling established companies — to join 24 Health Moonshot Communities ranging from Women’s Health to Food as Medicine (see full list and application links below).

“These aren’t just ordinary founder communities,” says StartUp Health CEO & Co-founder Steven Krein, “Each Health Moonshot Community unites 100% mission-aligned founders and CEOs with the bold goal of solving one of the biggest health challenges of our time.
Whether you join one of the listed Health Moonshot Communities or aim to launch a new one with us, genuine dedication to impact is key.
Attitude, Energy & Collaboration: We seek “batteries-included” individuals with a proactive spirit and positive energy.
“As we have since our founding in 2011, we’re looking for founders with the Health Transformer Mindset ,” says StartUp Health president and co-founder Unity Stoakes.

“These are people who are committed to their health moonshot, recalibrate regularly, and uplift others.” The new communities build on the success of the T1D Moonshot Community, supported by The Helmsley Charitable Trust, and the Alzheimer’s Moonshot, backed by Gates Ventures and ADDF, the Alzheimer’s Drug Discovery Foundation.

“I love connecting with other CEOs going through the same thing you're going through and so we can bounce ideas off of each other,” says Warren Marcus, PhD, CEO and founder of WiNK Therapeutics and a member of StartUp Health’s T1D Moonshot.
Learn more about StartUp Health’s annual membership program and apply to join a Founder Intro Session at startuphealth.com/membership .

Craig Ritchie Is Optimistic About StartUp Health’s Alzheimer’s Moonshot Community « Back to Health Transformer Journal Jul 30 Written by Nicole Kinsey Craig Ritchie, MD, PhD, a leading figure in Alzheimer's research and a member of StartUp Health's Alzheimer's Moonshot Impact Board, challenges your perception of Alzheimer’s as he shares his insights and experiences in the field.

Ritchie highlights his journey from psychiatry to spearheading major research initiatives, emphasizes the importance of innovation and collaboration in finding a cure for Alzheimer's, and shares his optimism for StartUp Health’s Alzheimer's Moonshot Community.
His journey began in 1997 in Melbourne, focusing on Alzheimer's disease, drug discovery, and development.
Ritchie iscusses the role of cardiovascular health, diet, and lifestyle, highlighting that risk factors for dementia and early Alzheimer's disease may differ.

It’s not the physician’s fault, they just don’t have many tools in their toolbox for early stage cognitive decline.
Usually the response from the healthcare provider is to simply watch and wait until things get worse.
Some of the most prominent apps that target early stage dementia or mild cognitive impairment use something called cognitive stimulation therapy or cognitive test therapy.
“You learn the task itself.” For Kiwit, a serial entrepreneur and digital health expert based in Berlin, that problem begged for an answer.
Origin Story Nina Kiwit studied economics in Germany, but after school fell in love with the startup life.
She worked at big startups in eCommerce but quickly realized she wanted to have a more lasting impact in the world.
She got an advanced degree in digital health at the Hasso Plattner Institute and Mount Sinai New York and dove into electronic health records and machine learning.
She has served as COO of multiple digital health startups.
While well understood in depression therapy, behavioral activation therapy is a relatively new concept for treating early-stage cognitive disorders.
In 2018, researchers in the United States conducted a large-scale clinical study in which they adapted the approach for older people with cognitive impairment and dementia.
The app includes an AI assistant named after Barry Rovner, MD, the doctor who proved the efficacy of the therapy in the United States.
